parts.title: Mathematical & PyTorch Foundations
description: Every language model is a cascade of matrix multiplications, probability distributions, and gradient updates. If you can read code, you already have the instinct this part builds on: you want to trace the numbers by hand and watch the mechanism run.

We start with tensor shapes and linear algebra, derive backpropagation and probability from first principles, and assemble a complete PyTorch training loop. Everything here earns its place in the Transformer and training chapters ahead.

parts.title: Inside the Transformer & Language Modeling
description: A language model turns raw text into token IDs, mixes context across positions through attention, and outputs a probability distribution over the next token. Follow that forward pass closely and every architectural choice has a concrete cause.

We move from subword tokenization into scaled dot-product attention, rotary positional encoding, Pre-LN normalization, and the full Transformer block, then finish with decoding strategies and perplexity.

parts.title: Modern Architectures Beyond Dense Text
description: Dense text-only Transformers are only the starting point. Frontier models decouple parameter count from active compute, replace quadratic attention with recurrent state spaces, fuse vision with language, and generate images by reversing noise.
These four chapters trace Mixture of Experts, Mamba state-space models, vision-language multimodal architectures, and diffusion models down to their core equations and memory tradeoffs.

parts.title: Retrieval, Embeddings & Grounded Evaluation
description: Private knowledge changes on its own schedule and never sat inside pretraining weights. Grounding answers means keeping source facts intact from chunking and embedding through approximate nearest-neighbor search and generation.

We build the full retrieval stack from chunking, cosine similarity, and HNSW/IVF vector indexes to production RAG pipelines, then test outputs rigorously with benchmarks, model judges, and hallucination checks.

parts.title: Pretraining, Fine-Tuning, Alignment & Reasoning
description: When prompting and retrieval reach their ceiling, you change the weights. Each training stage, from compute-optimal scaling to post-training alignment, has its own numerical traps and failure modes.

We follow scaling laws, CUDA execution, mixed precision, FSDP/ZeRO sharding, SFT, and LoRA into reward modeling, RLHF, DPO, verifiable-reward reinforcement learning (RLVR), and test-time reasoning compute.

parts.title: Agents, Tool Use & Reliability
description: A model can propose a tool call or a multi-step plan, while your runtime owns what actually executes. Turning free-form completions into dependable workflows requires typed schemas, bounded control loops, curated context, and explicit trust boundaries.
These five chapters build reliable agents from constrained generation and function calling through ReAct planning, context engineering, and prompt-injection defense.

parts.title: GPU Kernels & High-Throughput Inference Serving
description: A model that works in a notebook still has to serve concurrent users under strict latency and memory limits. Inference is where HBM bandwidth, KV-cache fragmentation, scheduling, and low-bit precision become one coupled systems problem.

We measure TTFT and decode throughput first, then eliminate every bottleneck in order: FlashAttention, PagedAttention, continuous batching, speculative decoding, quantization, and GPU fleet autoscaling.

parts.title: Language Models, Evaluation & Applications
description: A model can sound sure and still be wrong about the document in front of you. Look at the text it actually received, the representations it built, and a check that tells you whether the answer is usable.
With that, you can put together tools, retrieval, safety checks, and evaluations you can defend. The later chapters on model internals and serving are easier once you know what the system is for.

parts.title: Transformer Architectures & Attention
description: When an application depends on a model, a bad token often comes from inside the forward pass. The model may have skipped a position, hidden the wrong context, or flattened the scores before decoding.
Stay with one representation as it moves through embeddings, attention, images, position, and normalization, until it becomes the next token.

parts.title: Pretraining, Fine-Tuning & Alignment
description: A model that is almost right is a good reason to teach it something more specific. You want an example that changes the behavior, and a test that confirms the change is real.
The chapters here cover scaling laws, pretraining data, precision, distributed training, adapters, preferences, verifiable rewards, reasoning, and distillation.

parts.title: Autonomous Agents, Tool Protocols & Sandboxing
description: Giving a model a tool is the easy part. The engineering work is deciding what your runtime trusts, remembers, isolates, and retries.
These chapters take retrieval and tool use into vector indexes, GraphRAG, working memory, sandboxing, recovery, and multi-agent orchestration.

parts.title: High-Throughput Inference & Serving Systems
description: Once many requests arrive together, KV-cache memory, batching, kernels, and scheduling determine how the product feels.
Follow a request through FlashAttention, PagedAttention, continuous batching, speculative decoding, quantization, CUDA kernels, and autoscaling.

parts.title: System Design & Production Codebases
description: A chapter can be right on its own and still cause trouble beside the rest of the system. Serving changes the latency budget; retrieval changes what the model may claim.
The final chapters assemble full end-to-end architectures and inspect canonical open-source systems from PyTorch and vLLM to FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, NCCL, and Megatron.

parts.title: Math, Tensors & Deep Learning Foundations
description: Every model rests on tensor shapes, linear algebra, gradients, probability, and clean PyTorch training loops.
Start with small hand-checked numbers and build neural networks from scratch before scaling up.

parts.title: Classical Machine Learning & Evaluation
description: Fitting the rows you trained on is easy. Knowing whether a model generalizes to new data requires clean splits, sharp metrics, and disciplined experiments.
These chapters build core predictive models and evaluation habits that carry directly into LLM engineering.

parts.title: Language Models, Evaluation & Applications
description: Trace text through tokenization, contrastive embeddings, the Transformer block, decoding, prompting, RAG, and rigorous evaluation.

parts.title: Transformer & Multimodal Architectures
description: Look inside attention, RoPE, LayerNorm, Mixture of Experts, Mamba, Vision Transformers, multimodal fusion, diffusion, and mechanistic interpretability.

parts.title: Pretraining, Fine-Tuning & Alignment
description: Scale, adapt, and align language models with scaling laws, CUDA, mixed precision, FSDP, SFT, LoRA, RLHF, DPO, RLVR, reasoning, and distillation.

parts.title: Advanced Agents & Retrieval
description: Build vector indexes, GraphRAG, working memory, isolated sandboxes, failure recovery, and multi-agent workflows.

parts.title: GPU Systems & LLM Inference
description: Eliminate serving bottlenecks from KV caches, FlashAttention, PagedAttention, and CUDA kernels to quantization and fleet autoscaling.

parts.title: System Design & Production Codebases
description: Design production AI systems end to end and read the architecture of PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, NCCL, and Megatron.
